Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Burundi has a functioning judicial system with general court oversight of government actions. No ID-specific judicial oversight mechanisms have been identified.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Cited DPI Map page was fetched and does not mention judicial oversight at all (it lists only ID/payment/exchange technical fields) so it does not actually support this score. Independent check of Burundi's 2018 Constitution (arts 231-238) confirms a Cour Constitutionnelle and administrative courts with general powers of judicial review over state acts, but no ID-specific judicial review mechanism was found. Score of 2 (general oversight, not ID-specific) is confirmed on better evidence; original citation flagged as inadequate.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: Citizens can open bank accounts and mobile money accounts using national IDs per UNCDF 2025. The CNI is accepted but not mandatory for banking; other documents are also accepted. No e-KYC framework exists.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed by a second, companion UNCDF 2025 report (Payment Infrastructure Assessment), which independently states citizens can open bank and mobile money accounts using national IDs, with other documents also accepted for the purpose. Score of 2 (accepted but not mandatory) is corroborated by two independent primary-source documents.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: The CNI is mandatory for all Burundians aged 16 and older. Age 16 falls within the 10-17 range on this scale.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Source directly confirmed: IRB Canada research (citing Burundi's Isôko government portal and an Embassy of Burundi official) states the CNI is mandatory from age 16, which sits in the 10-17 bracket. Note that the new biometric ID being rolled out in 2026 is still awaiting its governing law (Burundi Times, 7 May 2026), so the minimum enrolment age for the new digital credential specifically is not yet confirmed and should be re-checked once that law is adopted.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: Coverage is estimated in the 20-49% range. The World Bank 2021 noted 27% of the population remains unregistered. The paper-based CNI system has significant coverage gaps especially in rural areas.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The cited 2021 World Bank figure (27% unregistered, i.e. ~73% coverage) refers to the paper-based CNI/civil register, not a digital ID credential — the 2022 World Bank project document itself confirms Burundi had no foundational digital ID system at that time. As of May-June 2026 Burundi has only just unveiled a biometric ID platform and is still awaiting enabling legislation before card production/distribution to the public begins (Burundi Times, 7 May 2026; BiometricUpdate, 30 June 2026), so actual digital ID population coverage is close to 0%. Revised to code 1 (<20%) to match the variable's definition (digital ID credentials issued/registered), which the original score conflated with paper-ID coverage.
